author: Cree Say
title: A SYMPHONY OF SECRETS The sins we hide series Book 4
text: someone breached our security system,and photographers were literally standing at our doors. We had to increase security and hire more personnel. The only person allowed in or out without chaos was Jordan. Sometimes he even stayed overnight because my paranoia had me checking every window and door at ridiculous hours. And Ray… my sweet, tiny chaos queen… She is an adorable attention seeker. Every time we go out on the balcony for fresh air and the paparazzi start snapping photos, she waves like she’s greeting her imaginary subjects. Then she giggles, proud of herself as if she just won an award. I can genuinely see her in the spotlight one day , that confidence is in her bones. Now she’s with me everywhere. Her nanny, Clara, too. I take her to rehearsals, to the studio, everywhere except interviews. She loves going because, well… her favorite human exists there. Jordan. And now she has Sammy wrapped around her little fingers, which is hilarious because Sammy used to claim he “doesn’t do kids.” I’m always alert though , wary of paparazzi and wary of Isaiah’s silence. His silence has always been the loudest warning. --- We finished our biggest show yet, the entire theatre packed. Every seat sold out the moment tickets dropped — even with the chaos swirling around my life. I bowed, waved, and picked up the single rose tossed onto the stage. When the curtains closed, I sighed, letting the adrenaline melt off my skin as I walked backstage. The first thing I heard was a squeal. “Mummy! So pretty!” Ray barreled toward me, tiny arms raised, her curls bouncing. Clara was behind her, trying to keep up. I scooped my girl into my arms, showering her cheeks with kisses as she giggled. “You think I was pretty, baby?” “Yes! Pwitty like pwetty princess!” She clapped her hands excitedly. If joy had a sound, it would be her laugh. I twirled her gently, and she shrieked happily, gripping my shoulders with her tiny hands. Jordan appeared from the side, leaning against the wall, smiling at us like we were his whole world. The man had the audacity to look soft. “Did Mummy do well tonight?” he asked her. Ray nodded so hard her curls slapped her face. “Mummy best! Best in da whool world!” I laughed. “You’re going to make me spoil you even more.” “You alweady spoil me,” she declared proudly. Jordan snorted. “She’s not wrong.” I shot him a look, and he walked closer, placing a kiss on Ray’s forehead before brushing his fingers lightly down my cheek. “You were beautiful out there,” he murmured. His hand slipped behind my waist, and he leaned in. I didn’t resist. His lips brushed mine , soft at first, then deeper , the kind that made warmth rush straight to my stomach. Ray giggled behind her little fingers. “Mummy kissing!” Jordan laughed against my lips. “Your daughter is a narc.” “I heard that,” Ray said dramatically, even though she definitely didn’t know what “narc” meant. I held her on my hip as Jordan leaned in again. This kiss was hotter, hungrier. My fingers curled into his shirt, and my heart thudded. God, if we weren’t in public, I’d drag him home and climb him like a tree— “DADDY!” A little voice cut through everything. Jordan stiffened instantly. We turned. A small boy , maybe six , sprinted toward us. Blond hair. Brown eyes. The same shade as Jordan’s. The resemblance slapped me. He wrapped himself around Jordan’s leg. Jordan froze. “Daddy! I found you!” My lungs stopped working. Jordan’s face drained of color. “Colton… hey, buddy… what are you doing here?” Son? My arms tightened around Ray instinctively. She sensed my body shift and tucked herself closer to me. Before Jordan could say anything else, a woman appeared behind the boy. Tall. Gorgeous. Dressed like she stepped out of a magazine shoot. Her eyes swept over Jordan… then me… then Ray… And her smirk sharpened. “Well,” she drawled, “I see you ran straight to your little show after the performance.” Jordan’s jaw clenched. “Why are you here? And why did you bring him without telling me?” She scoffed. “Our son wanted to see his father. You know… his father? The one who barely visits?” Ray frowned, burying her face in my neck. I swallowed hard. “Jordan…?” He turned quickly. “Alyssa, it’s not what she’s implying—” “Oh, don’t humiliate yourself,” the woman cut in sharply. She looked at me with fake sympathy. “Did he not tell you? About me?” Jordan snapped, “Stop.” She ignored him and kept going... “He loved to pretend he was single. He loved pretending he wasn’t sleeping in my bed while chasing someone else.” Jordan inhaled sharply. “That’s a lie. Alyssa, she’s twisting everything.” The woman raised an eyebrow. “Oh? Did you tell her how you ghosted your son? Or how you show up maybe twice a month , on good weeks?” Colton looked up at Jordan with sad eyes. “Daddy… you don’t want to see me?” Jordan’s voice cracked. “Of course I do. Buddy, I—” “You’re always with her now,” the woman continued, gesturing at me as if I were something stuck to her shoe. “The actress. The one with the baby. Playing house with someone else’s man.” My pulse thudded painfully. I stepped back, Ray clinging to me. Jordan moved quickly. “Alyssa, please don’t listen to her. She’s doing this on purpose.” The woman smirked , a wicked, victorious curve. The kind of smile that only appears when someone knows they’ve successfully delivered a fatal blow. “It’s always the same type,” she said casually. “The mistress pretending she didn’t know.” My throat burned. My chest tightened. Ray whimpered softly, confused and scared. Jordan reached for me. “Alyssa, please—” I stepped back. “No,” I whispered. “Not right now.” His face shattered. “Let me explain—” I shook my head. “I need to go.” The woman folded her arms smugly. “Run along, sweetheart. Next time choose a man who doesn’t already have a family.” Jordan barked her name... “ Kaya!Stop. Enough.” So now I knew her name. But I didn’t stay. I turned and walked away, clutching my daughter like she was the last piece of me not falling apart. Ray’s tiny voice trembled. “Mummy… don’t cry…” I didn’t even realize I was. Clara rushed to us, eyes widening. “We’re leaving,” I said, barely a whisper. She nodded instantly, guiding us out the back exit as Jordan yelled my name somewhere behind us. I didn’t turn around. I couldn’t. I walked out of the theater with my daughter in my arms, tears burning down my cheeks, while the man I was beginning to trust , beginning to fall for ,broke apart behind me. And just like that… My fragile new beginning shattered in one public, heartbreaking moment. Thirty One I stepped out into the back parking lot, my pulse still hammering in my ears, but even out here I could hear Jordan calling after me. His voice carried across the asphalt, closer than I wanted it to be. I didn’t even need to turn around to know he was chasing me, but I did anyway,and there he was, actually running toward me. And behind him? The woman. Kaya. Carrying the little boy whose name I’d barely managed to remember,Colton. My stomach clenched so hard it felt like someone had tied a fist around my ribs and squeezed. My mind kept circling one horrifying thought: He has a child. And not just that,he kept it hidden. For months. While he looked me in the eyes, held me, told me the kind of truths that felt like promises. I had been honest with him. I had given him all the soft, tender, trembling parts of me. And he,he’d been lying right to my face. God, I really was a fool. Here I was thinking he was different from these Hollywood men. Different from the glamorous, self-obsessed narcissists who cheated their way through promotions and parties and PR scandals. But apparently, he fit right in. Perfectly. Jordan reached me, out of breath, eyes wide with panic. “Alyssa, you can’t leave. I promise you—what she’s saying is all lies.” He stepped closer, but I held my ground. My voice shook, but not with weakness. “So the boy isn’t your son?” He gave me a look,pleading, cautious, terrified. But not truthful. “You don’t get it,” he whispered. “Please, baby… let me explain everything.” I jerked away when he reached to touch my arm. “Don’t touch me. And don’t call me baby. Explain what, Jordan? That you’ve been lying to me all this time while I trusted you? You can’t even answer my question. Is he or is he not your son?” Before he could respond, she caught up. Kaya arrived with a click of expensive heels and a cloud of perfume strong enough to resurrect the dead. She set Colton on the ground, smoothing his hair as he tugged at Jordan’s pants. Then she gave me a smile so sweet it should’ve come with a health warning. “I’m Kaya,” she said brightly. “Jordan’s wife—or should I say, baby mama. Didn’t get to introduce myself earlier.” Jordan stiffened. “No, you’re not. Kaya, I told you—” “Oh relax,” she cut in, waving a hand. “I’m just introducing myself. You must be Alyssa.” Her gaze dragged down my outfit like she was reading the price tags. “I’ve heard so much about you. From the internet… and the messy scandals.” Ray pressed her face into my shoulder, her tiny fingers curling into my sleeve. “Mommy, who’s that lady?” she whispered. Kaya perked up. “And this must be the little baby the internet keeps talking about.” She reached out as if to touch Ray’s cheek. Mistake number one. I stepped back so fast she nearly touched the air instead. “Don’t.” Ray buried deeper into me, smart girl that she was. Even at two years old, she could smell fake sugar coating a rotten core. Jordan immediately stepped between us, jaw locked tight. “Kaya, stop. What are you doing here? I told you to call before—” “Well,” she said with an innocent blink that couldn’t fool a blind man, “if you ever answered your phone, maybe I wouldn’t need to show up unannounced.” He swallowed. Hard. “I’ve been busy.” “With her?” Kaya tilted her chin in my direction like I was some charity case he’d picked up on the street. “And her baby?” "Daddy" Colton called out Jordan knelt to Colton, resting his hands on the boy’s shoulders. “Hey, buddy. I told you—you weren’t supposed to call me that out loud here.” Kaya let out a soft laugh. “Jordan, please. He’s a child, not a trained guard dog. He misses you. Let him call his father what he wants.” Ray tensed again. She peeked up over my shoulder, her big green eyes studying Jordan, studying the boy, studying everything. Then she whispered something that nearly cracked me open. “Mommy… Daddy?” Everything inside me froze. We didn’t say that word in my home. Amy and I had shielded both Emeric and Ray from that word because it came loaded with too much pain. Too many memories. Too many scars we weren’t ready to reopen. And now Ray had heard it. Now she was looking at Jordan like he was a hero in a story she didn’t understand yet. Jordan’s eyes instantly softened. He reached a little toward her. “No, sweetheart,” he said gently. “I’m not your—” “She knows who her father is,” Kaya cut in, sugary sweet. “And clearly so does your son.” Oh, she was playing dirty. And she was enjoying every second. Jordan snapped toward her. “Enough, Kaya.” “Why?” She shrugged, all faux innocence. “Alyssa deserves to know you’ve been lying to her. You’re good at compartmentalizing, but this?” She smiled, brittle and poisonous. “Even for you, this is impressive.” Ray looked between all of us, confused and frightened. I straightened, tightening my hold around her small body. My own pulse thudded painfully. “Jordan,” I said softly but firmly. “Is any of this true?” His lips parted, and he looked absolutely terrified. “Alyssa… please. Let me explain. It’s not what she’s making it sound like.” Kaya raised her brows. “Really? So you didn’t have an affair with your father’s wife? You didn’t get me pregnant? You didn’t drop off the face of the earth while you played house with her in New York?” For a second, my world tilted. “What?” I whispered. His father’s wife? What in God’s name…? That explained her maturity, her energy, her entire smug performance. Jordan’s hands trembled. “Kaya—” Colton frowned up at him. “Dad? Are you in trouble?” Jordan flinched like he’d been shot. And that was it. That was the moment everything clicked painfully, like bones snapping out of place. The tension. The hesitation. The secrets he kept dodging. The nights where something haunted him but he’d never say what. I had spent months choosing him. Trusting him. Allowing myself to fall, knowing how badly I could break. And he didn’t tell me about this. Jordan reached for me again. “Alyssa, please don’t walk away. Not like this. Just give me a second—” But I was already opening the car door. I gently handed Ray to Clara, who immediately lifted her into the seat to buckle her in. Ray pressed her forehead against my collarbone, sensing every ounce of my unraveling. “Mommy home?” she whispered, voice trembling. “Yes, sweetheart,” I managed, though my throat was tight and aching. “We’re going home.” “Jo-jo coming?” she asked softly, trying to peek around me to see him. My heart twisted, but I kept my voice steady. “No, baby. Jo-jo’s not coming.” “Alyssa,” Jordan pleaded, sounding absolutely broken. “Don’t go. Just let me talk. I’m begging you.” “I asked you,” I whispered, “if you were keeping anything from me. You said no.” He looked like I’d stabbed him. “I didn’t tell you because I was scared. I didn’t want to lose you.” “Well,” I said painfully, “you have now.” He moved toward me again. “Alyssa, I swear—” “Oh please,” Kaya muttered, rolling her eyes. “Let her go, Jordan. She’s just your latest distraction. She’ll find another man to play baby daddy soon enough.” Something cold and lethal shifted inside me. Jordan snapped. “Shut your mouth.” But I was already done. I got into the car, carefully, making sure not to push him too hard while his son was right next to him. I closed the door, started the engine, and rolled down the window. “I don’t ever want to see you anywhere near my daughter or me,” I told him, my voice low, steady, final. “No—Alyssa, no! Please, just let me explain!” he said, stepping toward the window. But I was already pulling away. “We are not done, Alyssa!” he shouted across the parking lot. “You’re my girl! I’m not letting you go that easily!” Ray sniffled softly in the back seat. “No cry, Mommy.” “I’m sorry, baby,” I whispered. “Mommy’s just sad.” “Ice cream make it go ‘way,” she offered gently, hopeful. I let out a broken laugh. “Thank you, sweetheart.” “Luv you, Mama.” “I love you too, baby,” I whispered, my voice cracking for real this time. And just like that, I drove toward the city lights with yet another breaking heart. Thirty two Jordan I didn’t move. Not when her taillights disappeared. Not when the sound of her engine faded. Not even when the cold slammed into my chest like someone had carved me open and left my ribs exposed. I just stood there. Kaya was saying something behind me , I didn’t care. Colton was tugging my sleeve asking if I was okay , I couldn’t answer. The parking lot, the people, the damn buzzing streetlights… everything blurred. All I could see was her. Alyssa. Leaving me. Driving away with her daughter , with our daughter in all the ways that mattered , while I stood frozen like a coward who’d run out of excuses. God. I messed this up. I messed everything up. I pressed my hands to my face. My palms were shaking. My throat burned. My stomach twisted so violently I thought I’d throw up right there on the pavement. The air felt too thin, too sharp, like I wasn’t allowed to breathe it anymore. Because the only person who made breathing feel easy had just told me she never wanted to see me again. I deserved it. But fuck, it still ripped me apart. “Jordan,” Kaya said somewhere behind me, voice fake-sweet and grating. “You can drop the dramatics now. She’s gone.” I turned around so fast she flinched. “Get out,” I said quietly. She blinked. “Excuse me?” “I said get out. Now. Leave.” Colton looked up at me with wide eyes. “Daddy… you’re scaring me.” The word “Daddy” stabbed through me again — but now for a completely different reason. I crouched down to him, brushing a hand through his hair. “Hey, buddy. It’s okay. I’m not mad at you. I’m just…” Breaking. Dying. Losing the one person I’ve ever loved without needing to pretend. “I’m just having a rough moment,” I said instead. Kaya rolled her eyes. “Really? Over her? You barely know—” “Get. Out,” I repeated, standing. She scoffed, grabbed Colton, and strutted off toward the elevator, mumbling something about me being dramatic. I didn’t watch them leave. I couldn’t. Because the second they were gone, I folded. My hands braced on the hood of the nearest car as everything I’d been holding in, years of shame, guilt, panic, every secret I buried , detonated inside my chest. The sound that came out of me wasn’t human. It was a broken, strangled thing I didn’t know I was capable of making. She left. She left. The one person I thought I might finally be worthy of… And it was my own damn fault. I slammed my fist into the metal. The car shook. Pain shot
